title: Lever lock
prompt: a key-operated lever lock beside its key on a table with three buttons: “Insert” slides the key beneath the tumblers; “Turn” aligns their slots and extends the bolt; “Wrong key” leaves a tumbler blocking the bolt; see-through reveals the spring-loaded levers, stump, bolt pin and key profile
blurb: A five-lever teaching adaptation shows how a matching key aligns gates so the bolt stump can pass.

limits: Enlarged colour-coded schematic, not exact book geometry or a manufacturable lock.
Animation stages key lifting and bolt drive for readability.
Bolt travel uses a drawing scale of three units per millimetre.
Insert after an attempt replaces the specimen and matching key as a teaching action. It is not hardware self-repair.
1988 is access-restricted and unverified. 1998 is not individually verified. No complete edition union is claimed.

citations.scope: Conventional pivoted lever, gate, spring, fence and bolt principles only. Extra anti-pick mechanism is not reproduced.

verification.productionTelemetry: n/a. Standalone static figure has no production telemetry.
verification.views: Seven yaw/pitch samples, both opaque and see-through; actual turntable start/stop and Front view interactions.

video.review: Reviewed initial state, real clicks, matching-key bolt extension, wrong-key block, replacement specimen, rotation and phone frames.
